gen-gf-bonbon-archivo: Inviting and personal, Bonbon sets thick pen-and-paper letters up top, while Archivo opens its curves outward beneath it. Bonbon is best for a few warm words; Archivo handles the rest.
gen-gf-bonbon-fs-asap: Bonbon brings thick, handwritten letters with a friendly, pen-and-paper feel. Asap, a sans with body height nearly matching its capitals, reads smoothly, though it is happiest in brief stretches rather than page after page.
gen-gf-bonbon-fs-epilogue: Personal and inviting, Bonbon lays down heavy, pen-and-paper letters with a thick strip through the middle. Epilogue, a sans-serif with a wire-like monoline skeleton and curvy, unclamped letters, keeps things light for a quick look.
gen-gf-bonbon-fs-erode: Erode moves like an editorial serif, with a tall middle band and gently shifting stroke weight. Bonbon does the warm, handwritten hello best, while Erode carries a few dignified lines but not long paragraphs.
gen-gf-bonbon-fs-fira-sans: Chunky handwriting up top, a tidy sans below. Fira Sans holds every stroke uniform with a large x-height, which lets Bonbon stand out as loose handwriting in a brief line.
gen-gf-bonbon-fs-hind: Inviting and personal, Bonbon is thick, handwritten, and loose. Hind, a sans with strokes like a drawn string and lowercase nearly matching its capitals, reads steadily but is best kept to brief spells.
gen-gf-bonbon-fs-public-sans: Public Sans brings a hefty lowercase and broad open counters, so it holds firm beside thick, handwritten Bonbon. And since neither wants long paragraphs, a generous size for Bonbon makes the most of the pairing.
gen-gf-bonbon-fs-supreme: Chunky handwriting meets crisp type, with Bonbon up top and Supreme underneath. But as text piles up, Supreme's open letters keep moving, while Bonbon prefers only a brief line.
gen-gf-bonbon-general-sans: Bonbon arrives thick, handwritten, and full of pen-and-paper charm. Bonbon greets best, while General Sans, with a tall x-height and smooth curves, does the steadier work in short runs.
gen-gf-bonbon-manrope: A thick, heavy strip of handwriting runs through Bonbon, loose and pen-and-paper personal. Manrope, drawn in rods with bright open curves, keeps things light, so a few lines never feel crowded.
